docs.title: analint
docs.text:
Declare how a system behaves in Python, then check its consistency.

Describe state with entities, transitions with actions, and relationships with invariants. Run concrete scenarios or explore the reachable states to find a counterexample you did not think to write as a test.

pip install analint
analint check path/to/spec/

Requires Python 3.12 or newer. This guide targets analint 0.2.0, including enum lookup, floor division, one-sided saturation and the reachability and diagnostic repairs. The site tracks the main branch; check your installed version with analint --version. Read the 0.2.0 migration notes before upgrading. To run this checkout from source:

git clone https://github.com/angru/analint
cd analint
uv sync --frozen
uv run analint check examples/cloak/

docs.title: Start with a small model
docs.text:
The first-spec tutorial builds a ticket workflow with three reachable states. You will check a successful transition, an intentionally blocked transition, a complete journey and a reachability property, then introduce a defect and read its counterexample.

Your next step Read Understand what a PASS proves Verification concepts Look up a declaration or semantic rule DSL reference Run checks, inspect a model or read JSON CLI reference Give a coding agent the workflow or connect MCP For AI agents Learn from a larger working model Examples gallery

docs.title: What the checker establishes
docs.text:
analint checks the model you declare: its state domains, actions, guards and initial states. A complete exploration can prove safety and reachability within that model. It does not verify that application code implements the specification, and NoDeadEnd establishes that a goal remains reachable rather than that every execution eventually reaches it.

Results distinguish PASS, FAIL and INCONCLUSIVE. A budget-exhausted check cannot silently become a pass. Individual properties can also be NOT_CHECKED when they could not be evaluated. See verdicts and completeness before using the checker as a CI gate.

The project is an early public release; pin a version if you depend on its API. Development and release history live in the roadmap and changelog.

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text:
analint is built for coding agents as first-class users: every command speaks JSON with a versioned schema, and the model is inspectable without reading source. There are two ways to give an agent that surface.

This page documents the repository's main branch. cache is available since 0.0.3; the other listed MCP operations are available since 0.0.2. The CLI reference covers terminal options, which are not identical to the MCP argument set.

docs.title: Agent Skill (recommended)
docs.text:
The repository ships a portable Agent Skill at skills/analint/. A skill is a plain SKILL.md that teaches an agent when and how to use analint: the show → affects → what-if → apply → check loop, fail-closed verdict interpretation, and the DSL's semantic rules (effects are simultaneous facts, where to put Field/Invariant/Lifecycle, Scope/Param/presence, the loader contract). It carries no scripts — the CLI already owns execution.

SKILL.md is an open format read natively by Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot; Antigravity and other agents that scan a skills/ directory pick it up the same way.

Install — copy the skill into the agent's skills directory:

# Claude Code: project-local or global
cp -r skills/analint .claude/skills/analint
# or  ~/.claude/skills/analint

# Codex / Antigravity: into that agent's skills directory

The agent also needs analint on PATH:

pip install analint        # or: uv add analint

Then drive it in plain language — "use analint to check this spec before editing" — and the skill supplies the workflow.

docs.title: MCP server (optional)
docs.text:
For clients that prefer typed tool discovery over a shell, the same core is exposed as an MCP server with five tools — check, show, affects, explore, trace:

pip install "analint[mcp]"   # then configure `analint-mcp` in the client

Use MCP when the client benefits from discoverable, typed operations or has no normal shell; otherwise the CLI plus the skill is the lighter path.

Configure a local stdio server in your client's MCP settings with executable analint-mcp and no arguments. The process must have access to the spec files and its required Python imports. The exact settings-file format belongs to the client. Paths are resolved on the machine running the server; use absolute paths when the client's working directory is uncertain.

docs.title: Tool reference
docs.text:
0.1.0: every MCP tool request loads the current model sources in a fresh worker, so edits to entry points and imported modules are visible without restarting the server. Python class identities are shared within the request. The in-process loader still caches imports; use a fresh process for library calls that must observe edited source files.

All five tools return structured dictionaries. Optional arguments and defaults below match the server's tool definitions.

Tool Required arguments Optional arguments check None path=".", what_if=null, max_states=null, slice=true, tlc=false, cache=false, compact=false, checks=null, scenario_ids=null, tags=null, tlc_timeout=null show None path=".", kind=null, name=null affects target path="." explore None path=".", query=null, what_if=null, include_graph=false, max_graph_states=null trace A property id in query for a useful request path=".", query="", what_if=null, slice=true, max_states=null, cache=false, tlc=false, tlc_timeout=null

check runs the full validation pipeline. max_states overrides every exploration budget and must be positive; slice=false corresponds to CLI --no-slice. tlc=true tries the supported TLC fallback for INCONCLUSIVE properties. MCP exposes no strict parameter; use the CLI when that policy is needed. 0.1.0: checks selects flow/query/invariant ids without removing system actions. scenario_ids/tags add filtered scenarios, and tlc_timeout bounds each TLC run. None selects the usual full check; an empty checks list or unknown/ambiguous ids return an analint.error/v1 usage error. Qualified ids (flow:ID, query:ID, invariant:ID) resolve collisions. See the selection contract, including dependency-related supporting proofs and the selected-scope JSON metadata. For explicit selections, model_findings contains unrelated diagnostics encountered during bounded exploration. These are outside the selected verdict. Unreleased: sliced selections limit action exploration to selected checks and dependencies. Check selection.unassessed_actions for actions whose transition defects and fireability were outside coverage. Trace returns the same selection metadata. An unfiltered check covers the full model.

Since 0.0.7, use compact=true to receive counts and up to three examples per finding group. The report keeps each group's check context, severity and expected rejection marker. Use compact=false to retrieve every finding. See the compact JSON format.

show returns an overview without a kind, an id list with just a kind, and details with a kind/name pair. Detailed kinds are entity, event, invariant, query, action, lifecycle, flow, scenario and contract. affects accepts a field, entity/event name or action id.

Impact reports include Create initialization, RHS/payload expressions and implicit presence/terminal guards. Inspect action presence_reads and presence_writes or entity presence_read_by/presence_written_by for membership changes; ordinary field reports describe field values. See the impact contract for default initialization and static-read semantics.

Since 0.0.6, show(kind="query", name=ID) returns the query type, predicate/goal, declared budget and declarative roots without enumerating states. show(kind="action", name=FAMILY_ID) accepts an unexpanded family name from a Contract and returns kind: "action_family", parameters, where, the shared contract and concrete variant ids. Use a concrete id for bound action details. See the CLI inspection contract for fields and root inheritance. On released 0.0.5, use overview query ids and read declarations for their details; actions require concrete expanded ids.

A what-if file can import the entry through analint_spec, but objects owned by other package modules need their original imports, such as from oauth.protocol import tokens.

explore follows the whole model for canonical or query-specific roots. It returns a compact artifact by default. To request the graph, supply both include_graph=true and max_graph_states=N; the latter caps output, not exploration. Above that graph size, the response retains the summary and explains why graph is null. Read completeness separately.

trace accepts an invariant id as well as a query id, despite the argument's name. It follows the same slice and budget decisions as check. A property without a witness returns witness: null with an explanation. Invocation settings do not carry over between calls. 0.1.0: pass the same max_states, slice, cache, tlc and tlc_timeout to trace. Both tools share the selection/execution pipeline. A TLC-decided trace returns the parsed action_trace and explicitly reports unavailable state snapshots; native traces keep their state changes. See trace output.

For example, send these arguments to check:

{
  "path": "/absolute/path/to/ticket_spec",
  "max_states": 10000,
  "slice": true
}

Then inspect the witness by passing this to trace:

{
  "path": "/absolute/path/to/ticket_spec",
  "query": "can_archive"
}

docs.title: Workflow and verdicts
docs.text:
1. show the inventory, then inspect the relevant action or contract.
  2. Use affects before changing a field or transition.
  3. Test a proposed property through check(what_if=...) using the same packaged entity imports as the model.
  4. Apply the accepted change and list its behaviour on Spec or Contract.
  5. Run check again and read the overall verdict and per-property findings.

The check response uses analint.check/v1. Treat only verdict: "PASS" and passed: true as success; FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE and individual NOT_CHECKED results require interpretation. Scenarios passing does not establish canonical invariants. A retrieved trace is diagnostic evidence, not a substitute for the full report. See verification concepts.

CLI consumers must read the response, not just the process exit: trace exits zero when it successfully reports a FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE property. For check, an exhausted budget normally gives INCONCLUSIVE/exit 4; --strict promotes its warning to overall FAIL/exit 1 while retaining per-property INCONCLUSIVE status.

docs.title: JSON schema identifiers
docs.text:
Response Schema Validation report analint.check/v1 Validation report with grouped findings analint.check.compact/v1 Model inventory analint.overview/v1 Detailed object or id list analint.show/v1 Impact analysis analint.affects/v1 Exploration artifact analint.exploration/v1 Witness/counterexample analint.trace/v1 Operation error, where supported analint.error/v1

Classify findings by their code rather than message text, and skip findings marked "expected": true (the intended rejection in a passing Expect.FAIL scenario) when routing failures; see finding codes. Finding codes and expected rejection metadata are available since 0.0.6.

Inspect error fields as well as schemas. Some lookup errors retain the operation's schema. Invariant traces identify the property with invariant instead of query; clients should accept both forms.

docs.title: Which to use
docs.text:
Layer Job analint CLI / library the executable source of truth Agent Skill teaches an agent when and how to use analint MCP server typed, discoverable operations with structured results

The skill and the JSON schemas are versioned (analint.check/v1, analint.show/v1, analint.exploration/v1, …) so an agent can detect stale instructions. Validation is always mandatory: a skill is prompt text, not a typed guarantee.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: The examples below use the tutorial model. Replace . with a directory containing spec.py or the path to an entry-point Python file. Run analint --help or analint COMMAND --help for installed-version options.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
analint check .
analint .                         # shorthand
analint check . --format json
analint check . --format json --compact
analint check . --strict

Checks loading and structure, scenarios, flows, canonical invariants and queries. The overall verdict includes all of these stages.

Option Meaning -f, --format terminal\|json Select human-readable or JSON output --compact Group and sample findings in JSON output (requires --format json) --check ID 0.1.0: select a flow, query or invariant; repeat or use KIND:ID -s, --scenario ID Filter scenarios by id; repeat for multiple ids -t, --tag TAG Filter scenarios by tag; repeat for multiple tags --strict Warnings fail the run --what-if FILE.py Merge hypothesis objects for this invocation --max-states N Override canonical and query budgets with a positive integer --no-slice Use whole-model exploration instead of property slices --tlc Hand supported INCONCLUSIVE properties to TLC --tlc-timeout SECONDS Timeout per exported TLC check, at least 1 second; default unlimited --cache Since 0.0.3: persist/reuse explorations of unchanged slices

Scenario/tag filters select scenario execution; they do not turn the command into a scenario-only validation that skips invariants, flows or queries.

docs.title: Selecting checks over one model
docs.text:
Available in 0.1.0.

--check changes the checks to run, not the system being checked. It retains all declared actions, constraints and roots. For example, from a source checkout:

analint check benchmarks/shared_checks.py --check checkout
analint check benchmarks/shared_checks.py --check release_reservation
analint check benchmarks/shared_checks.py --check query:shipment_keeps_reservation
analint check benchmarks/shared_checks.py --check checkout --check can_ship --max-states 100

Without --check, the existing full-check behavior remains. With it, only the named flows/properties and their supporting checks run; add --scenario/--tag to include matching scenarios. Scenario ids and tags intersect as before. Unknown ids/tags, ambiguous check ids, and filters matching no scenarios fail as usage errors (exit 2). Bare check ids must be unique across flows, queries and invariants; flow:ID, query:ID and invariant:ID disambiguate. Repeated selectors are deduplicated.

Structural validation always covers the whole model, including unselected behavior. Flows keep their own given; queries keep their declared roots or the canonical initial relation. No selection changes roots or mutates budgets.

An explicit --check run proves only dependency-related supporting invariants. With slicing, selected AlwaysHolds and Unreachable queries first attempt a proof without invariant pruning. A complete, applicable PASS with legal roots and no transition errors discharges that query's supporting invariant proofs. With --tlc, TLC can complete a capped attempt. Counterexamples, evaluation errors, exclusions, unsupported exports and other unsuccessful attempts use the ordinary constrained pipeline; a speculative counterexample is never reported as a real failure without rechecking it. Reachable witnesses retain constrained path validation, and explicitly requested invariants are still proved.

This works with canonical or query-owned roots. An own-root safety proof is independent and never borrows or grants canonical invariant trust. Other queries request dependency proofs as before; the set grows when invariant constraints are needed. An invariant proved without constraints needs no further support. This is a dependency analysis, not logical minimization of predicates. Budgets can affect which proof strategy succeeds and therefore which supporting checks are needed. --no-slice uses a conservative constrained dependency closure and still explores the whole state space.

The verdict and exit code aggregate requested checks, their supporting proofs, and relevant transition defects. Unreleased: sliced selections explore the selected and supporting slices, with action-slice defect coverage seeded by their dependencies. A clean unconstrained safety proof supplies its own coverage. For example, analint check benchmarks/independent_checks.py --check safe_a passes and identifies bump_b as unassessed. The unfiltered check still fails on B's invariant. Flow-only requests check applicable invariants at each step and skip global exploration.

Findings outside the selected dependencies that are encountered during this work still go into model_findings. These findings retain severity, code, location and trace text and affect neither the selected verdict nor --strict. model_coverage reports bounded reachability coverage, including root sets, exploration/state counts, caps and excluded actions. The counts include reused graphs and successful safety proofs and exclude unsuccessful speculative attempts. model_coverage.scope is selected_slices_from_verification_roots for sliced selections (including whole-model fallbacks) and actions_from_verification_roots with --no-slice.

Structural errors, load failures and invalid declared initial relations remain blocking. Every invariant still participates in initial-state legality: an illegal root affects the requested verification even when the invariant reads other fields. 0.1.0: when exploration reports that same illegal root, its duplicate non-blocking model diagnostic is suppressed using recorded state provenance. The blocking root failure remains. Later violations and diagnostics without matching provenance are retained; sharing a code or invariant location is not enough to merge them. Full reports may therefore contain several paths to the same invariant. Use --compact to group these findings without treating the group count as a count of unique defects. NoDeadEnd retains global support because any invariant violation can strand a full-model state; DeadActions asks about all actions. Unknown dependency analysis falls back to the whole model. No action or invariant is removed from the model.

Filtered JSON reports add selection (also in compact mode): requested, supporting, not_selected, dependencies, full model_actions, action_coverage, selected-scope excluded_actions, effective options and budgets. Explicit check selections also list covered_actions (included in bounded reachability coverage at one or more verification root sets) and unassessed_actions (outside that coverage). Transition defects and fireability of unassessed actions are outside the report's reachability scope. Actions excluded within the covered slices are listed separately in model_coverage.excluded_actions. Dependencies identify actions and constraints used by each check, including whole-model fallback. Caps and exclusions can limit coverage within a slice. A successful unconstrained safety proof can establish absence of defects on its slice. Its graph may include paths that invariant pruning would block, so inclusion in covered_actions alone establishes no fireability verdict. Found witnesses and counterexamples remain conclusive.

Each sliced check spends its budget on its own dependencies. For example, a safety check with a large budget and a witness check with a small budget can both pass even if extra exploration would find a defect in an action only the witness depends on. With --no-slice, the safety check's larger whole-model exploration can discover that defect, which then blocks the combined verdict when the checks share verification roots.

A selected PASS establishes only its reported scope. --strict still applies to warnings in verdict-bearing sections, including structural warnings about the whole model. Scenario/tag filters without --check retain full-check behavior. Run an unfiltered check for full validation. A selection is only as cheap as its slices: when a selected property's slice spans most of the model (for example, 32 of 33 actions because every action touches a shared balance), the selection explores about as much as a full check and is not faster. An unsuccessful safety attempt can add work before the constrained retry. benchmarks/safety_bridge.py demonstrates a passing local safety query whose bridge constraint would otherwise pull in broken, unrelated proofs. The selected run passes while the unfiltered run fails; no system actions are removed.

The cache directory defaults to ~/.cache/analint; set ANALINT_CACHE_DIR to override it. Caching does not change findings or completeness. Timings measure performed work, so a reused exploration is cheaper than a fresh one.

docs.title: JSON reports
docs.text:
check --format json returns analint.check/v1. Read verdict and passed before inspecting individual results. passed is true only for an effective PASS, including the effect of --strict.

Field Contents spec Root id and name load_errors, structural Load problems and structural findings scenarios, flows Example/journey results and findings invariants, queries Per-property status, state count, trace and findings exploration Findings encountered while exploring transitions summary Aggregated counts, including inconclusive and unchecked invariants

Property results can include slice, elapsed_ms and backend: "tlc". elapsed_ms measures incremental work for that property; shared exploration is charged to its first consumer, and invariant retries are included. Query timing includes safety attempts (even discarded attempts) and action coverage requested by that query. Model preparation and invariant-phase shared action coverage are excluded. Summing these timings does not give total command time.

Unreleased: invariant and Unreachable results with a projection attempt include a model object. Its relation is over-approx for a projected safety proof, under-approx: replayed for a concrete violation confirmed by replay, exact for a deciding exact retry, or null when the retry is inconclusive. The object lists the system ID, root source and numbers, retained fields, dropped elements with reasons, ordered attempts and the exact recheck when one was needed. Each attempt records its backend, budget, completeness, status and explored state count. The projected attempt's status is local to its graph. Its proof_blockers list explains transition defects, evaluation errors, or budget exhaustion that prevent transferring a proof to the system. Candidate traces are local to the attempt. A trace on the check itself is concrete and a replayed trace may be longer than the shortest witness. slice continues to describe an exact slice. When exact diagnostic coverage already explored that slice, its state count can still appear in states_explored. Read the deciding attempt for the proof's own state count. A selected --check can prove PASS when the same obligation in a full run is INCONCLUSIVE. The projected graph can complete within budget even if the exact graph caps, or prove that excluded actions leave all retained fields and slot presence unchanged. Full runs retain exact per-check budget and exclusion behavior. --no-slice uses only the whole model. TLC checks only exact graphs.

0.1.0: a tlc.transition_defect finding is retained in the affected query or invariant's findings and repeated in exploration. The first occurrence attributes the defect to that check; the second makes the aggregate run FAIL (exit 1), even if the target itself stays INCONCLUSIVE because TLC stopped at the transition defect. This applies to both full and selected checks. These are two report locations for the same defect, not evidence of two distinct bugs. Concatenating sections or adding compact group counts does not produce a unique defect count; the report does not provide global diagnostic identities.

An empty reachable prefix is rendered as (initial state) → paint, including the attempted action. Non-empty prefixes keep their action sequence. The defect path is diagnostic text, not a proved witness or counterexample for the target: trace retains the blocking finding and aggregate FAIL while the target can remain INCONCLUSIVE with no property witness or state trace.

docs.title: Compact findings
docs.text:
Since 0.0.7, check --format json --compact returns analint.check.compact/v1. Within each finding list, entries are grouped by code, severity and expected. Each group reports its full count and up to three examples in report order. Each example contains the original location and message. An expected: true group represents intended rejections in a passing negative scenario.

Both formats include the validation verdict, summary and individual check results, and use the same exit codes. Use check --format json for every individual finding in analint.check/v1.

docs.title: Finding codes
docs.text:
Since 0.0.6, every finding is {"severity", "code", "location", "message"}. Classify findings by code, not by message: wording may change, but within analint.check/v1 a code is never renamed or reused for another kind. New codes may be added, so treat an unknown code by its severity. Exploration artifacts (analint.exploration/v1) carry the same codes.

A finding inside a passing Expect.FAIL scenario that gives the rejection reason has "expected": true. Its ERROR severity is preserved, but it is the intended outcome, not an actionable failure. The key is absent everywhere else, and it never appears in a failed scenario. Verdicts and statuses are unchanged.

Prefix Codes finding. finding.unclassified (the default for findings constructed without a code via analint.reporter.Finding) structural. structural.empty_model, structural.missing_id, structural.duplicate_id, structural.duplicate_class, structural.unregistered, structural.stale_reference, structural.invalid_entry, structural.scope_misuse, structural.unbound_variable, structural.effect_conflict, structural.unknown_field, structural.lifecycle_unattached, structural.terminal_transition, structural.unreachable_lifecycle_state, structural.no_scenarios, structural.missing_given, structural.duplicate_given, structural.empty_flow, structural.payload_binding, structural.payload_type_mismatch, structural.conflicting_roots, structural.invalid_initial model. model.unloaded_file, model.orphan, model.canonical_initial_error transition. (rejections) transition.pre_failed, transition.pre_not_applicable, transition.presence_rejected, transition.terminal_locked transition. (model defects) transition.evaluation_error, transition.field_constraint, transition.undeclared_lifecycle_edge, transition.postcondition_violated exploration. exploration.action_excluded, exploration.unsupported_value invariant. invariant.violated, invariant.evaluation_error, invariant.not_checked scenario. scenario.expected_rejection, scenario.not_rejected, scenario.then_failed, scenario.then_evaluation_error, scenario.event_not_emitted flow. flow.step_not_run, flow.invariant_violated, flow.checkpoint_failed, flow.checkpoint_evaluation_error, flow.event_not_emitted query. query.invalid, query.invalid_root, query.invalid_state, query.evaluation_error, query.vacuous, query.witness, query.holds, query.reached_forbidden, query.not_reachable, query.property_violated, query.dead_end, query.goal_unreachable, query.dead_actions, query.not_assessed, query.undecided, query.initial_state check. check.budget_exhausted, check.excluded_actions tlc. tlc.unavailable, tlc.no_invariant_form, tlc.not_exported, tlc.failed, tlc.transition_defect, tlc.decided

docs.title: show
docs.text:
analint show -p .
analint show action -p .
analint show action resolve -p .
analint show query -p .
analint show query can_archive -p .
analint show entity Ticket -p .
analint show lifecycle Ticket.status -p .
analint show action redeem_code -p examples/oauth/

show [KIND] [NAME] --path PATH always returns JSON. Without arguments it returns the analint.overview/v1 model inventory. With a kind it lists ids; with a kind and name it returns details using analint.show/v1.

Detailed kinds are entity, event, invariant, query, action, lifecycle, flow, scenario and contract. Singular and plural kinds work for id lists, including show query / show queries and show entity / show entities.

Since 0.0.6, show query ID returns kind: "query", the query type, label, effective max_states (query override or inherited Spec budget), predicate and goal. The predicate is null for NoDeadEnd/DeadActions; the goal is populated only for NoDeadEnd. This describes the check without running it; use check for a verdict and trace for a witness or counterexample.

The roots object describes the query's starting relation. Its source is canonical when the query inherits Spec.initial or entity defaults, and query when it declares its own given, given_any or initial. It includes rendered given / given_any snapshots (Absent(ref) preserves absence) and the effective initial relation: vary, where, given, max_candidates. A null initial means defaults plus any given snapshots. Candidate states are not enumerated and the relation is not validated by inspection.

Since 0.0.6, show action FAMILY_ID accepts an unexpanded parameterized family name, such as redeem_code from oauth-protocol. It returns kind: "action_family", the declaration's shared pre/effect/post/emits, parameter params with rendered domain values, where, variant_count, concrete variants ids and related scenario/flow ids. Only variants already in the model are listed, after static where filtering; an empty family remains inspectable with zero variants. This does not expand or execute the family again. A concrete action id keeps kind: "action" and its existing detail format, taking precedence over a family name if both match.

docs.title: affects
docs.text:
analint affects Queue.open_tickets -p .
analint affects Ticket -p .
analint affects resolve -p .

affects TARGET --path PATH returns analint.affects/v1. Targets are fields (Entity.field), entity/event names or action ids. Inspect readers, writers, constraints and scenario coverage before changing the model.

Since 0.0.5, field writers include Create initialization, including omitted fields taking their defaults. Such entries carry initialization: "explicit" or "default" and render the Create(...) operation. Delete changes presence rather than assigning field values. Entity written_by includes both creation and deletion.

Reads cover pre/post predicates, effect right-hand sides, old Add/Subtract targets, emitted payload expressions, lifecycle transition source states and terminal locks. These are static dependencies across possible worlds, not a claim that every expression executes in every state. Payload/post references describe next-state dependencies; they need not read the old value of a field the same action assigns. World invariants are listed separately from action reads.

Action reports add presence_reads (instance labels) and presence_writes ({"instance": "Item['a']", "present": true|false}). These cover explicit Present predicates, scoped field reads, finite quantifier/aggregate membership and the implicit guards for modifying/creating/deleting a slot. Entity reports add presence_read_by and presence_written_by; their ordinary reader/writer lists also include presence dependencies. Field reports remain about field values. Key(ref) alone reads neither fields nor presence; quantification over keys still reads domain membership. Expression-based event bindings and their scenarios are included. These are additive fields in the existing v1 schemas.

0.1.0: if a --what-if file cannot be loaded, both explore and trace return a load error (exit 3), just as check rejects that preparation. They do not return an artifact for the unchanged base model.

docs.title: trace
docs.text:
analint trace can_archive -p .
analint trace can_archive -p . --format json
analint trace resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket -p .

trace PROPERTY_ID --path PATH returns a query witness or invariant counterexample with state changes. Options are --format terminal|json, --what-if FILE.py and --no-slice. 0.1.0: --max-states, --cache, --tlc and --tlc-timeout accept the same invocation settings as check.

JSON uses analint.trace/v1, with query or invariant identifying the property, its status, the root, steps and final_state. A property without a witness returns witness: null and an explanation. The command follows check's slice and budget decisions; use --no-slice for the whole model. 0.1.0: pass the same budget/cache/TLC options used for the selected check. A trace call selects that one property plus the same supporting invariant proofs; it does not inherit settings from a previous process. query:ID and invariant:ID disambiguate. trace accepts only queries and invariants: a flow:ID selector copied from --check is not a valid trace target and returns an unknown-property error. Run that flow with check --check flow:ID instead.

0.1.0 trace metadata includes selection, verification_verdict and exploration findings. Unrelated findings and their bounded coverage appear in model_findings and model_coverage, with the same verdict separation as check. A property's status does not override failures in its supporting verification. TLC checks defect assertions only for the selected proof's dependency actions; all exported actions and legal-state constraints stay in the transition system. When TLC decides the property, backend: "tlc" and action_trace retain its parsed witness (null means no witness; [] can mean the initial state). TLC state snapshots are not available: state_trace_available is false, root is null, steps is empty and final_state is empty. The tool does not substitute a native rerun or invent state changes. Native traces retain the existing state-diff representation. A query.invalid_root failure includes an explanation in message: the root is invalid under model invariants and was not expanded. Native traces retain that root with zero steps; TLC includes its number and explanation without state snapshots.

NoDeadEnd uses query.invalid_state when its chosen dead-end witness has explicit invariant-violation or invariant-evaluation-error provenance. Its message names the invariant ids and explains that the state was not expanded; recovery from that invalid state was not assessed. The query remains FAIL and the invariant diagnostic remains visible separately. Native trace retains the same witness and steps and includes this explanation in message. Legal dead ends keep query.dead_end; no-goal and incomplete-graph results retain their existing diagnostics. Attribution uses finding-to-state indices, including on warm cache reads, never diagnostic prose or a matching invariant id alone.

Successful trace retrieval is an inspection operation. Its process exit code does not replace the property's status or a check verdict.

docs.title: explore
docs.text:
analint explore .
analint explore . --format json
analint explore . --query can_archive --format json --include-graph

explore [PATH] explores the whole model, starting from canonical roots or the roots of --query ID. It accepts --what-if FILE.py and --format terminal|json. --include-graph includes the nodes and edges in JSON; the default is a compact summary.

The analint.exploration/v1 artifact includes source, completeness, summary, findings and graph. graph: null can mean output was intentionally omitted; it does not by itself mean the exploration was incomplete. Read completeness separately. The artifact's content-derived node/edge ids are stable across equivalent runs.

Like trace, explore is an inspection operation; use check as the CI verdict gate. Explore does not have the check command's --max-states, --cache, --tlc or --no-slice switches.

docs.title: Hypothesis workflow
docs.text:
Use the same shared entity classes in your hypothesis and spec. Packaged models use qualified imports, as shown in the tutorial.

analint show -p path/to/spec
analint affects Entity.field -p path/to/spec
analint check path/to/spec --what-if hypothesis.py --format json
# Apply the accepted change to the spec, then check again.
analint check path/to/spec --strict

--what-if merges objects without editing the entry point or permanently changing its cached root. After applying a hypothesis, list new behaviour on Spec or an imported Contract; normal module imports do not register it.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The following table applies to check:

Code Meaning 0 Effective PASS 1 FAIL: findings, failed scenarios/flows/properties, or strict warnings 2 CLI usage error, such as an invalid option or format 3 Spec failed to load or no root spec was found 4 INCONCLUSIVE, including an unchecked invariant preventing PASS

For show, affects, trace and explore, a successful response means the inspection operation ran; inspect the returned data to interpret verification results. Machine-readable operation errors use analint.error/v1 where supported.

docs.title: CI and local development
docs.text:
For an installed release, gate your spec with:

analint check path/to/spec --strict --format json

Pin the analint version and retain both the exit code and report. Do not turn code 4 into success without an explicit policy for unresolved properties.

From a repository checkout, the documentation is checked with:

uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_documentation.py \
  tests/test_fixed_initial.py::test_fixed_roots_across_check_explore_and_trace \
  tests/test_keys.py::test_key_verdicts_traces_artifacts_and_cache_agree
uv run --frozen --group docs mkdocs build --strict

The docs workflow performs these checks for pull requests and main-branch pushes before its main-branch-only deployment.

docs.title: Verification concepts
docs.text: A specification is a model of state and transitions. Verification asks what can happen under all enabled action choices from the declared initial states. Results depend on the completeness of that model: an omitted action, guard or domain case can make the model prove a property the real system does not satisfy.

docs.title: Scenarios, flows and exploration
docs.text:
Check Starts from Establishes Scenario Its concrete given snapshot One action accepts or correctly rejects this example Flow Its concrete given snapshot This sequence of actions and checkpoints executes successfully Canonical invariant verification Spec.initial, or defaults Each listed invariant holds throughout reachable states Query Its own initial source, otherwise the canonical roots The reachability or safety property for those roots

A passing scenario covers that example. A passing flow shows one executable journey. Neither establishes that all other action orders are safe; that is what the reachability engine examines.

Scenarios and flows have partial worlds: only supplied entity instances are present, and omitted scoped slots are absent. Canonical exploration starts with entities constructible from defaults and scoped slots present by default. Supply required field values and explicit Absent(ref) snapshots through an initial relation or a query's given when needed. A missing required default can prevent canonical verification even though all scenarios pass.

Since 0.0.4: Scope(..., initially_present=False) opts into absent defaults for canonical/query worlds. Explicit snapshots override the scope policy; each query-owned initial source starts independently from those defaults. Scenario and flow partial worlds keep the same behavior. See the identity and presence example.

docs.title: Initial states and domains
docs.text:
Spec.initial=Initial(vary=[...], where=[...], given=[...]) declares a finite set of canonical roots. vary enumerates field domains; where filters combinations; given fixes other field values or supplies instances without defaults.

Domains can come from booleans, enums, lifecycle states, bounded integer fields or Field(values=[...]). A BoundField in vary expands over its scope. max_candidates limits candidate generation; exceeding it is an error, never a truncated selection of roots.

Since 0.0.4: omit vary (or use vary=[]) for a fixed relation: Initial(given=[...]) builds one candidate from defaults plus those snapshots. where still applies, so a false filter yields an error rather than a vacuous PASS. Initial() selects the defaults-built world. This does not require enumerating finite domains for fields that stay fixed. Versions before 0.0.4 require a non-empty vary. See the fixed-root example.

A query can specify one of given, given_any or initial:

  • given=[...] supplies or overrides instances in the defaults-built root.
  • given_any=[[...], [...]] enumerates admissible roots explicitly.
  • initial=Initial(...) generates them declaratively.

Without its own initial source, a query uses the canonical roots. Multi-root queries must satisfy their requirement for every admissible root; for Reachable, each root must have a path to a matching state. A trace records which root it starts from. For a passing multi-root Reachable, the trace is one representative witness; the verdict checks every root, including paths that merge. A complete failure identifies an initial state with no path (a native trace has that root and zero steps). Missing paths under a capped or excluded transition relation remain INCONCLUSIVE. TLC checks projected roots separately; its state count sums those runs, and its timeout applies to each export.

An initial state that violates an invariant, or whose invariant cannot be assessed, is retained but not expanded. Root legality keeps the overall verdict FAIL, including selected checks. If a complete Reachable failure refers only to such roots, query.invalid_root explains that reachability was not assessed from the invalid root. If a legal root also has no path, its ordinary missing-path diagnostic takes precedence. Native traces retain the invalid root with zero steps; TLC traces carry the explanation without inventing state snapshots.

Unreleased (#65): even if a retained invalid root already matches the goal, Reachable does not use it as a positive witness. A complete check reports FAIL with the same invalid-root explanation. Capped/excluded proofs still remain INCONCLUSIVE and predicate evaluation errors remain errors. Projection may choose a legal representative of an equivalent root projection; its witness is legal, while the original root-legality failure still blocks the overall result. Unreachable retains its existing forbidden-state contract.

Unreleased (#66): TLC fallback reuses projected full-model root legality. Inert roots are assessed locally with the native predicate/error rules; only legal roots launch TLC. Mixed-query state counts include locally assessed roots, but only actual TLC runs produce backend notes. A later legal missing path still takes precedence, and backend errors or transition defects remain visible.

Numeric annotations alone do not bound a domain. An increasing int counter without an upper bound may generate infinitely many distinct states. Use finite abstractions and explicit bounds that reflect the requirement. Ordinary hard bounds reject an out-of-range transition with a finding; saturate=True clamps values at the thresholds and therefore changes the model's meaning.

docs.title: Verdicts and completeness
docs.text:
The command's overall verdict has three values. Individual invariant and query results can additionally report NOT_CHECKED.

Result Meaning Overall consequence PASS The check established its requirement for the model and roots Can contribute to overall PASS FAIL A counterexample, evaluation defect or other failure was found Overall FAIL INCONCLUSIVE The available exploration did not settle the property Prevents overall PASS NOT_CHECKED The property could not be evaluated, for example because no canonical initial state could be built Prevents overall PASS

An existential witness can settle a reachability check before the graph closes; universal safety or unreachability requires sufficient complete coverage. A concrete defect can fail a capped run. A property applicable in zero states cannot silently pass: vacuous queries fail, while an invariant never evaluated is NOT_CHECKED on a complete exploration and INCONCLUSIVE on a capped one.

Automatic invariant verification and scenario checks are distinct. An invariant whose direct entity/slot references are absent from a scenario is skipped there; finite quantifiers instead range over the present members. Empty ForAll is true; empty Min/Max is an evaluation error. Include the required data when using scenarios to exercise a rule.

For check, JSON passed is true only for an effective PASS. --strict makes warnings fail the run. Exit codes are documented in the CLI reference.

docs.title: Transition semantics
docs.text:
All execution paths use one transition kernel. Preconditions and terminal/presence guards can reject an action before effects. Effects apply simultaneously: every right-hand side reads the pre-state. The checker then checks postconditions and state invariants. A state violating an invariant is retained as a counterexample but is not expanded further.

An action cannot modify any field of an entity whose lifecycle is terminal, or delete that terminal entity. Two effects writing the same field are a structural error. Reading or modifying an absent scoped instance is rejected.

Expect.FAIL passes only for an intended pre-execution rejection. An effect error, failed postcondition or failed then assertion is still a failed scenario. Events are materialized observations; emission does not automatically dispatch another action. Exploration excludes actions requiring external event payloads and reports them as unassessed rather than falsely declaring them dead.

docs.title: Slices, budgets and repeated checks
docs.text:
By default, check explores each invariant or query on its cone of influence: the state it reads, the actions that can affect it, and the dependencies of those actions. Independent processes need not pay for their full Cartesian product. JSON records the slice. check --no-slice uses the whole model instead.

Spec.max_states bounds canonical invariant exploration and supplies the default budget for queries, including queries with their own roots. An explicit query max_states overrides that default. check --max-states N overrides all budgets for that invocation. An exhausted budget preserves INCONCLUSIVE. Raising the budget can help a large finite model, but cannot close an unbounded domain.

trace follows the property exploration used by check; trace --no-slice selects the whole-model path. explore always explores the whole model for its chosen roots. Sliced traces keep out-of-slice fields at their root values. One documented difference is that whole-model NoDeadEnd counts a state illegal under an out-of-slice invariant as a dead end, while that slice does not; the invariant violation still fails the run in its own check.

Since 0.0.3: check --cache persists explorations by a digest of the slice, roots, budget and engine source. An unchanged slice can reuse work across runs; model changes invalidate the relevant entries. The cache returns the same semantic findings as a fresh run. Check timing can change because it measures work actually performed, and shared work is charged to its first consumer.

docs.title: Projected safety proofs (Unreleased)
docs.text:
Sliced verification can first check an invariant or Unreachable on a projection of its effective initial states. It follows every expanded writer of a retained field and keeps inputs to visible updates, postconditions, payloads and lifecycle checks. It erases hidden writes and can weaken a precondition by removing a conjunct that reads an erased field. The projected graph covers every reachable concrete state for the retained fields.

A complete, error-free result with a legal, applicable concrete root can prove safety. Checks over scoped contents use exact execution when no applicable root contains a retained slot. The budgeted attempt leaves world-invariant pruning disabled. A projected counterexample describes a candidate path. The checker tries that path from the matching concrete roots with the original transition kernel and world invariants. When the exact retry reaches its budget, a replayed violation still establishes failure. The checker keeps exact action coverage for transition diagnostics. Full checks also retain their exact per-check budgets and reporting statistics. Selected checks can finish the property proof on the smaller graph. Unsupported projections and unsuccessful proofs use the existing exact verification pipeline.

docs.title: TLC fallback
docs.text:
check --tlc hands supported properties left INCONCLUSIVE to TLC on the same slice. It requires Java and a TLC jar, selected by ANALINT_TLC_JAR or a discovered Quint/Apalache installation. Use --tlc-timeout SECONDS to bound each exported check. A result decided by TLC carries backend: "tlc". 0.1.0: selected safety queries can first use an unconstrained proof attempt, including TLC when requested. Only a clean PASS discharges support; all other attempts return to constrained verification. Own-root attempts never inherit canonical invariant trust. See check selection.

The exporter mirrors the transition kernel and refuses constructs it cannot represent. Unsupported exports and timeouts leave the property INCONCLUSIVE. Current fallback supports invariants and Reachable, Unreachable and AlwaysHolds; NoDeadEnd and DeadActions are not exported. Floats, Min/Max and unsafe absent-slot reads are examples of export restrictions. 0.1.0: emitted payload constraints use the same post-state, nullable and non-clamping rules as native verification. A transition defect found by TLC makes the run FAIL; the target property's status can remain INCONCLUSIVE when TLC stops before deciding it. Defect diagnostics show the reachable prefix and attempted action. Custom event constructors and literal strings colliding with the reserved __null__ representation remain explicit export refusals. TLC is an additional verifier for the same finite abstraction; it does not turn an unbounded or incomplete model into a proven system.

docs.title: Recoverability and scope boundaries
docs.text:
NoDeadEnd(goal=...) asks whether a path to the goal exists from every reachable state. A system can satisfy this while repeatedly choosing a loop and never finishing. The query establishes recoverability, not liveness, fairness or termination of every execution.

analint does not model scheduling fairness, real time, probabilities, unbounded collections, automatic event delivery or concurrency inside one action. Model finite state alternatives explicitly and keep these assumptions visible. It also does not check that implementation code conforms to the model.

docs.title: DSL reference
docs.text: Import public declarations from analint. The first-spec tutorial is a complete runnable model; snippets below illustrate individual declarations and may refer to names defined there or in the linked examples.

docs.title: Migrating to 0.2.0
docs.text:
When upgrading from 0.1.0, review these changes before comparing old results.

  • Queries whose max_states is omitted or None now inherit Spec.max_states. An explicit query budget still takes precedence over the spec, and an invocation override takes precedence over both. Set max_states=10_000 on a query to keep the previous independent default. A changed budget can change whether a check completes; INCONCLUSIVE is still not a proof.
  • saturate=True now enforces values and exclusive gt/lt constraints after clamping. Models that previously relied on those constraints being skipped can report transition defects. The new saturate="low" and saturate="high" modes clamp only the selected inclusive bound and keep other constraints hard.
  • Multi-root Reachable requires a path from every admissible root. A witness from only one root no longer proves the query. Invalid roots remain blocking failures; their diagnostics now explain why exploration did not expand them.
  • Native checks support composing Lookup and //. TLC supports a narrower, provable integer domain: it refuses Lookup(...) // n, division of a field written by Lookup, and dynamic divisors. Unsupported exports remain INCONCLUSIVE instead of approximating the expression.

The older 0.1.0 migration notes still apply when upgrading from 0.0.x. Stable check ids and CLI exit codes are unchanged.

docs.title: Migrating to 0.1.0
docs.text:
When upgrading from 0.0.x, review these changes to the verification contract.

  • Operand literals are limited to None, bool, int, float, str, Enum and instance references. Declared Entity classes remain valid identities in parameter filters. Opaque Python objects are structural errors, including Decimal and date values that previously worked in native comparisons. Convert both literals and model field values consistently: for example, represent fixed-precision amounts as integer minor units with explicit rounding at the input boundary, and calendar dates as integer day ordinals or an explicit finite enum. Do not replace exact decimal arithmetic with floats indiscriminately. Define finite bounds for explored numeric domains. These are modeling choices; the checker does not convert values automatically.
  • Use And, Or and Not for symbolic expressions. Replace Python and/or/not and chained comparisons such as 0 <= Account.balance <= 100 with And(0 <= Account.balance, Account.balance <= 100). Boolean conversion now raises instead of silently losing part of a condition.
  • Selected checks put unrelated defects encountered during exploration in model_findings, outside the selected verdict. Unreleased: sliced selections list actions outside action coverage in selection.unassessed_actions. Read model_coverage for the bounds on coverage.
  • Handle INCONCLUSIVE (CLI exit 4), including when excluded event-subscriber actions prevent a proof. Do not infer success from an absence of counterexamples.
  • TLC can find a transition defect while the target property stays INCONCLUSIVE. The overall check can still FAIL (exit 1). Property and aggregate sections may repeat that defect for attribution; their counts are not a unique-defect total.

docs.title: State: Entity and Field
docs.text:
Subclass Entity and annotate fields. An instance carries values; a class-level field is an expression used in predicates and effects.

from analint import Entity, Field


class Wallet(Entity):
    balance: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=5)


Wallet(balance=3)       # concrete snapshot
Wallet.balance >= 1    # predicate, evaluated against a state later

Fields without defaults are required in snapshots. Unknown, missing required or constraint-violating values are rejected at construction.

Field option Meaning Field(default, ge=..., gt=..., le=..., lt=...) Numeric constraints, checked on snapshots and transitions Field(default, values=[...]) Explicit finite scalar domain Field(default, ge=..., le=..., saturate=True) Clamp numeric effects at both bounds Field(default, ge=..., le=..., saturate="low" / "high") Clamp only the selected bound; other constraints remain hard Lifecycle(...) as a field default Initial value, allowed edges and terminal states for a state field

Booleans, enums, lifecycle states, bounded integers and explicit value domains can supply finite choices to Initial. Numeric bounds define the abstraction: use thresholds deliberately, especially with saturation.

docs.title: Predicates and expressions
docs.text:
Comparisons ==, !=, <, <=, > and >= build predicate values. Fields and arithmetic expressions support +, - and *. Name expressions and predicates to reuse them; they are data, not callbacks.

from analint import And, Implies, In, IsNotNull, IsNull, Not, Or

can_pay = And(Wallet.balance >= Order.total, Order.total > 0)
remaining = Wallet.balance - Order.total

Use And(...), Or(...), Not(...) and Implies(a, b), rather than Python and, or, not or chained comparisons. In(field, values), IsNull(field) and IsNotNull(field) cover membership and null checks. Boolean fields can appear directly in predicate positions, such as pre=[Client.active].

docs.title: Invariant
docs.text:
Invariant(predicate, id="", label="") describes a state relationship.

from analint import Implies, Invariant

resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket = Invariant(
    Implies(Ticket.status != Status.NEW, Queue.open_tickets == 0),
    label="Resolving the only ticket clears the queue counter",
)

Listed invariants are automatically verified from the canonical roots and checked before and after scenario/flow actions where applicable. Direct reads of a missing instance make an invariant inapplicable to that snapshot. Quantified reads follow present scope members. Keep one-field constraints in Field; use invariants for relationships between fields or entities.

0.1.0: symbolic predicates, fields and arithmetic expressions reject Python truth-value conversion with a TypeError. Use And/Or/Not, and write And(0 <= Account.balance, Account.balance <= 100) instead of a chained comparison. This prevents Python from silently discarding part of a condition.

docs.title: Action and effects
docs.text:
Action(pre=[...], effect=[...], post=[...], emits=[...]) declares a transition. Metadata includes id, name, description and tags.

from analint import Action, Set, Subtract

pay = Action(
    pre=[Wallet.balance >= Order.total],
    effect=[
        Subtract(Wallet.balance, Order.total),
        Set(Order.paid, True),
    ],
    post=[Order.paid],
)
Effect Meaning Set(field, value_or_expression) The field has this value in the next state Add(field, amount) / Subtract(field, amount) Arithmetic forms of Set Create(ref, **fields) An absent scoped slot becomes present; omitted fields take defaults Delete(ref) A present scoped slot becomes absent

Effects are simultaneous: every right-hand side reads the pre-state, so list order cannot express a sequence. Two writes to one field are invalid. A slot cannot be created/deleted and also written by another effect in the same action. Use multiple actions in a flow when intermediate states matter.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Declare a lifecycle inline as a field default:

from analint import Lifecycle

status: Status = Lifecycle(
    initial=Status.NEW,
    transitions={
        Status.NEW: [Status.RESOLVED],
        Status.RESOLVED: [Status.ARCHIVED],
    },
    terminal=[Status.ARCHIVED],
)

Effects that change the field must follow a declared edge. terminal freezes the whole entity, including its other fields and deletion. Missing outgoing edges do not implicitly declare a terminal state. A declared edge out of a terminal state is a structural error.

docs.title: Scope, presence and instance references
docs.text:
A Scope(EntityClass, keys=[...]) allocates a fixed finite universe. Indexing returns an InstanceRef; ref.field addresses a particular instance and ref(field=value) creates its snapshot.

from analint import Absent, Present, Scope

wallets = Scope(Wallet, keys=["alice", "bob"])
alice = wallets["alice"]
bob = wallets["bob"]

alice_has_funds = alice.balance > 0
alice_exists = Present(alice)
# Snapshot entries: alice(balance=3), Absent(bob)

Use instance fields rather than ambiguous Wallet.balance once Wallet is scoped. Only one scope per entity type is supported. Absent(ref) marks a slot absent; Present(ref_or_bound_or_param) tests membership. Scenarios/flows omit slots as absent, while exploration defaults them to present unless overridden.

Ordinary field reads and writes need a present slot. Create requires absence, Delete requires presence; a mismatch rejects the action before effects. Keys never grow dynamically. Guard a possibly absent field read with And(Present(ref), ref.field == value) so absence does not cause an evaluation error.

docs.title: Declared keys and initial presence
docs.text:
The following APIs are available since 0.0.4.

Key(ref_or_param_or_bound) is a value expression returning the slot's declared key, with its original type. It accepts an InstanceRef, a Param whose entire domain consists of instance references, or a quantified Bound. Values may be None, booleans, integers, finite floats, strings or Enum members. Other hashable scope keys remain supported as identities but cannot be used with Key. Identity is independent of presence: Key(ref) works for an absent slot and reads no state. A Bound needs an enclosing quantifier/aggregate; an instance Param is substituted during action expansion. Static Action.where filters can compare keys. There is no automatic conversion between a scope key and a foreign-key field: use the same domain values, such as Enum members, in both.

Scope(..., initially_present=False) makes omitted slots absent when building canonical and query roots. The default is True, preserving existing models. Explicit ref(...) and Absent(ref) snapshots override the policy. Each query-owned given, given_any world or Initial is built independently from the scope defaults and its own snapshots; it does not merge canonical snapshots. Queries without their own source inherit the canonical worlds. Scenarios and flows continue to treat omitted slots as absent regardless of this policy. Varying a field of an absent slot remains an error; supply a present snapshot before including that field in Initial.vary.

This complete example starts with an empty scope, then records an absent slot's identity as the owner of a created slot:

scope-identity-spec.py
from analint import (
    Absent, Action, And, Bound, Create, Delete, Entity, ForAll, In,
    Invariant, Key, Not, Present, Reachable, Scenario, Scope, Spec,
)


class Item(Entity):
    owner: str = "none"


slots = Scope(Item, keys=["a", "b"], initially_present=False)
a, b = slots["a"], slots["b"]
x = Bound("x", slots)

create = Action(effect=[Create(b, owner=Key(a))])
delete = Action(effect=[Delete(b)])
safe = Invariant(ForAll(x, In(x.owner, ["none", Key(a)])))
query = Reachable(And(Present(b), b.owner == Key(a)))

created = Scenario(
    name="Create with the declared owner", action=create, given=[Absent(b)],
    then=[Present(b), b.owner == "a"],
)
deleted = Scenario(
    name="Delete an owned slot", action=delete, given=[b(owner="a")],
    then=[Not(Present(b))],
)

spec = Spec(
    id="scope-identity", name="Declared identity and empty initial scope",
    actions=[create, delete], invariants=[safe], queries=[query],
    scenarios=[created, deleted],
)

check proves the invariant and reaches the query through create; the complete graph contains two states. trace query shows Item['b'].owner becoming "a". The exploration/trace JSON schemas keep their existing scalar representation (Enum values use Type.MEMBER); model views add initially_present to scope metadata. TLC exports keys through its existing literal encoding. Unsupported values such as floating-point keys cause an explicit export refusal and leave the check INCONCLUSIVE; they are never approximated.

docs.title: Param: finite action families
docs.text:
Param(name, *domain) accepts explicit values, entity classes, enums, booleans or a scope. Param(name, ge=N, le=M) declares an inclusive integer range.

from analint import Action, Add, Param, Subtract

src = Param("src", wallets)
dst = Param("dst", wallets)

transfer = Action(
    params=[src, dst],
    where=[src != dst],
    pre=[src.balance >= 1, dst.balance < 5],
    effect=[Subtract(src.balance, 1), Add(dst.balance, 1)],
)

alice_pays_bob = transfer.bind(src=alice, dst=bob)

The declaration expands into ordinary bound actions when the Spec is built. where filters static parameter combinations; state-dependent conditions, including Present, belong in pre. List the family on Spec.actions. Param and parameter fields support +, -, * (including reflected forms) and all six comparisons directly; p + 0 wrappers are unnecessary. Use .bind(...) to select the concrete action for a scenario or flow. Do not generate model elements with Python factory loops; finite families belong in Param.

0.1.0: binding refreshes the concrete action from the current family declaration, including nested guard/effect/payload edits. Rebinding the same family and arguments preserves the action's identity so existing scenario and flow references still match Spec expansion. Those references see the refreshed contents; this is not an immutable model snapshot. Copied families own separate binding memos. Rebinding preserves established action IDs and family labels, including IDs assigned to bound variables by the loader. Unnamed bindings are named once their family is named. A discarded family no longer leaves its memo in a global store. Refresh happens on .bind(...) or a new family expansion, not automatically when an existing Spec is validated. Rebuild the Spec after changing parameter domains, where, or referenced model elements so membership/reference closure is current. Do not edit declarations during an active verification run.

docs.title: Bound, quantifiers and aggregates
docs.text:
Bound(name, scope) binds a variable over present instances of that scope.

from analint import Bound, Count, Exists, ForAll, Max, Min, Sum

wallet = Bound("wallet", wallets)
all_nonnegative = ForAll(wallet, wallet.balance >= 0)
someone_has_funds = Exists(wallet, wallet.balance > 0)
funded_count = Count(wallet, wallet.balance > 0)
total_balance = Sum(wallet, wallet.balance)

ForAll and Exists are predicates. Count, Sum, Min and Max are arithmetic expressions usable in comparisons or effect right-hand sides. A bound field must occur within its quantifier/aggregate, or in the supported Initial.vary position.

Empty present set Result ForAll True Exists False Count, Sum 0 Min, Max Evaluation error

docs.title: Initial
docs.text:
Initial(vary=[...], where=[...], given=[...], max_candidates=10000) enumerates admissible roots. given fixes values, and where filters combinations with ordinary predicates and aggregates.

Since 0.0.4: vary can be omitted or empty. Initial(given=[...]) starts with one candidate built from defaults plus the supplied snapshots, then applies where. Initial() uses the defaults alone. A rejected candidate leaves no roots and fails validation; an evaluation error also fails. Versions before 0.0.4 require at least one varying field.

from analint import Initial

starting_balances = Initial(
    vary=[alice.balance],
    where=[alice.balance >= 1],
    given=[bob(balance=0)],
)

Attach it to Spec.initial for canonical verification or to a query's initial for that query only. Candidate overflow and evaluation errors fail rather than silently removing combinations. See initial states.

docs.title: Fixed-root example
docs.text:
Save this complete source as spec.py with analint 0.0.4 or newer installed and run analint check .. Both slots start absent; creating one increments the counter. The required Limit value comes from given. An independent noise action shows why property slices can be smaller than analint explore .'s whole-model graph. already_created supplies its own fixed root and needs no action to find a witness.

fixed-root-spec.py
from analint import (
    Absent, Action, Add, Bound, Create, Entity, Field, Initial,
    Invariant, Not, Present, Reachable, Scenario, Scope, Set, Spec, Sum,
)


class Limit(Entity):
    max_created: int


class Counter(Entity):
    n: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=1)


class Item(Entity):
    units: int = Field(1, ge=1, le=1)


class Noise(Entity):
    on: bool = False


items = Scope(Item, keys=["one", "spare"])
one = items["one"]
spare = items["spare"]
item = Bound("item", items)

create = Action(
    pre=[Counter.n < Limit.max_created],
    effect=[Create(one), Add(Counter.n, 1)],
)
flip_noise = Action(pre=[Not(Noise.on)], effect=[Set(Noise.on, True)])
balanced = Invariant(Sum(item, item.units) == Counter.n)
created = Reachable(Present(one))
already_created = Reachable(
    Present(one),
    initial=Initial(given=[Limit(max_created=1), Counter(n=1), one(), Absent(spare)]),
)
create_once = Scenario(
    action=create,
    given=[Limit(max_created=1), Counter(), Absent(one), Absent(spare)],
    then=[Present(one), Counter.n == 1],
)
noise_once = Scenario(action=flip_noise, given=[Noise()], then=[Noise.on])

spec = Spec(
    id="fixed_initial",
    name="Fixed initial world",
    initial=Initial(given=[Limit(max_created=1), Absent(one), Absent(spare)]),
    actions=[create, flip_noise],
    scenarios=[create_once, noise_once],
    invariants=[balanced],
    queries=[created, already_created],
)

The canonical whole-model graph has one root and four states; the invariant and created each need only two states in their slices. Use analint trace created with -p . for the create witness, or analint trace already_created -p . for the query-specific initial-state witness.

docs.title: Event and Emitted
docs.text:
Event uses typed fields like Entity. Action.emits accepts an event class or a payload template whose fields bind to state expressions:

from analint import Emitted, Event


class PaymentRecorded(Event):
    amount: int


# On an action: emits=[PaymentRecorded(amount=Order.total)]
# In Scenario.then or Flow.steps: Emitted(PaymentRecorded)

Payload templates are type-checked and materialized against the post-state. Emission does not dispatch another action. A scenario can supply an Event instance in given to test an action with payload preconditions; such external inputs are not generated by reachability exploration. They are reported as unassessed.

0.1.0: a materialized payload that violates its event's Field constraints produces a transition.field_constraint defect rather than raising an exception. Scenarios and flows fail, including scenarios with Expect.FAIL; exploration reports the path and attempted action without adding an invalid transition. Resolution or constructor errors use transition.evaluation_error. Event payloads are validated without clamping, even with saturate=True; that option clamps state updates, not event construction. Bare event classes still carry no payload. TLC exports supported payload bounds and enumerated values as transition-defect checks over the post-state, including the kernel's acceptance of None. Invalid payloads reject the transition without clamping. A reachable TLC transition defect makes the run FAIL even if the requested predicate remains INCONCLUSIVE because TLC stopped at that defect; its diagnostic includes the attempted action. Custom event constructors, unsupported scalar bounds such as floats, and literal strings equal to the reserved __null__ sentinel are refused with tlc.not_exported rather than approximated.

One-sided saturation applies to effect results and Create, before postconditions. "low" requires ge; "high" requires le; True still requires both. The opposite bound, exclusive bounds and values remain checked after clamping. Initial snapshots and event payloads are validated without clamping.

docs.title: Boolean predicate values (unreleased)
docs.text:
BoolValue(predicate) turns a DSL predicate into an ordinary boolean operand. It also accepts a bare boolean field. This lets a parameterized action update flags without duplicating an action for each enum value:

from enum import Enum
from analint import Action, BoolValue, Entity, Or, Param, Set

class Method(Enum):
    CARD = "card"
    WALLET = "wallet"

class Client(Entity):
    card_deposited: bool = False

method = Param("method", Method)
deposit = Action(
    id="deposit",
    params=[method],
    effect=[Set(Client.card_deposited,
                BoolValue(Or(Client.card_deposited, method == Method.CARD)))],
)

CARD sets the flag; WALLET preserves its previous value. Every effect RHS reads the pre-state, including predicates inside BoolValue. Create fields use the same rule; emitted payload templates still read the post-state. Scope Params, quantifiers and presence guards bind normally. Reading an absent instance without a guard remains an evaluation defect. References inside the predicate participate in model closure, impact reports, slicing and cache identity.

Use True/False directly for constants. BoolValue does not accept Python callbacks or coerce Python truthiness. A raw predicate in Set remains invalid: wrap it explicitly. Duplicate writes to one target remain invalid; this API adds values, not conditional effect lists.

Native operands retain Python boolean/numeric semantics. TLC exports boolean values and equality/membership within proven boolean domains; it checks roots and writes instead of trusting annotations. It explicitly refuses numeric uses of BoolValue, mixed boolean/integer domains, ordered or null comparisons, and numeric field constraints on these values. Existing unsupported predicates (for example a Min/Max expression) still refuse export. A refused fallback remains INCONCLUSIVE with tlc.not_exported, never an approximated proof.

docs.title: Enum constant lookup
docs.text:
Lookup(Account.kind, {Kind.STANDARD: 60, Kind.PRO: 30}) is an integer-valued expression that composes with arithmetic, predicates and effects. The table must cover every member of one enum; values must be integer constants, excluding bool. The constructor copies the table. Params and quantified/scoped fields work as selectors. An unmatched selector raises an evaluation error, with no default arm. Scalar enums retain Python equality (IntEnum/StrEnum match their underlying values), consistent with ordinary DSL comparisons and state identity.

TLC exports literal enum selectors and fields whose roots and writes are known to contain members of that enum. It explicitly refuses other selector domains; this prevents scalar-enum encoding from hiding an invalid native selector.

docs.title: Integer floor division
docs.text:
Integer expressions support // and reflected forms (100 // Account.leverage), including Params, scoped fields and aggregates. The result rounds toward negative infinity: -5 // 2 == -3, 5 // -2 == -3. Integer operands produce integer results. Native evaluation follows Python numeric semantics, including bool/int and equal integer/float values; other operand types are rejected. TLC retains its existing integer-only numeric domain. A literal zero divisor is a structural error; a state-dependent zero divisor becomes an evaluation finding and fails the check.

TLC supports provably integer numerators and nonzero constant integer divisors (including bound Params). It checks root values and writes rather than trusting annotations; bool/float numerator domains and dynamic divisors are explicitly refused, leaving a capped check INCONCLUSIVE; no approximate division or ignored zero case is exported. / and % are not added.

docs.title: Scenario and Flow
docs.text:
Scenario(action=..., given=[...], then=[...], expected=Expect.PASS) checks one action. then accepts predicates and Emitted checks. Expect.FAIL expects pre-execution rejection, not a runtime defect.

Flow(given=[...], steps=[...]) executes a journey. Steps mix actions with Assert(predicate) and Emitted(EventClass) checkpoints. given is required; given=[] starts with an empty world. Only present instances are available, and each accepted step's state feeds the next step. A rejection or defect fails the flow. Both declarations accept id, name and description. A flow name is a display label in terminal, JSON and show flow; selection still uses its id. Unnamed flows retain their previous report shape. The tutorial shows complete examples.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Declaration Requirement Reachable(predicate) A matching state can be reached from each root Unreachable(predicate) No matching state can be reached AlwaysHolds(predicate) The predicate holds in every applicable reachable state NoDeadEnd(goal=predicate) A goal state remains reachable from every reachable state DeadActions() Assess which actions can never fire in the explored model

Each accepts id, label, max_states and one optional initial source: given, given_any or initial. Queries with none inherit the canonical roots. NoDeadEnd is recoverability, not a guarantee that every execution terminates. Excluded event-input actions are unassessed, not dead.

Unreleased. With slicing, NoDeadEnd can omit local boolean disablers when every affected flag has an always-available action that restores it. The goal and invariants must be independent of those flags, and terminal-lock dependencies are preserved. A complete, clean proof within the budget reports the smaller graph, with restorable_flags in its JSON slice summary. When the smaller graph cannot certify a pass, the full slice determines the verdict and any shortest counterexample and its diagnostics.

docs.title: Spec, Contract and loading
docs.text:
Spec(id=..., name=..., actions=[...], invariants=[...], scenarios=[...], flows=[...], queries=[...]) is the root. It can additionally list entities, events, scopes and lifecycles, which are otherwise derived from referenced behaviour. Spec.initial supplies canonical roots; Spec.max_states sets the canonical exploration budget and the default query budget (default 10,000). A query with max_states=None (the default) inherits this value, including with its own roots. An explicit query budget wins; check --max-states N overrides both for one run.

0.2.0: omitted query budgets inherit Spec.max_states rather than always using 10,000. Use an explicit max_states=10_000 on a query to retain the old budget. Inheritance is resolved per check, so a shared query can be used with different Specs without being mutated.

Contract(id=..., actions=[...], ...) is an explicit reusable fragment with the same content lists. Spec(imports=[contract, ...], ...) combines those lists with the root's own. Contract version is descriptive metadata, not a resolver that downloads dependencies.

Load one entry point: a spec.py directory or an explicit Python file. Multi-file models should be packages with __init__.py and relative imports. List behaviour explicitly: merely importing a file does not register its actions or properties. The loader names empty ids from variable names, warns about unlisted behaviour and unreachable files, and rejects multiple Spec roots in one import graph. An empty behaviour model is an error.

The taskboard and broker examples show composition. Use analint show contract ID -p PATH to inspect a contract's public surface.

docs.title: Reusing a Spec with invocation settings
docs.text:
Available in 0.1.0.

Keep actions, constraints, flows and properties in one root model. The Python verification functions take selection and budgets separately from that model:

from analint.validator import validate_spec

# spec is the same already-declared Spec on every call; explicit ids are required.
checkout_result = validate_spec(spec, checks=["flow:checkout"])
property_result = validate_spec(
    spec, checks=["query:shipment_keeps_reservation"], max_states=100, cache=True
)
full_result = validate_spec(spec)

validate(path, checks=[...]) provides the same contract for a loaded file. Neither function edits the declaration lists, query budgets or fixtures. Results with a selection describe its scope; only that scope is established by PASS. Structural checks always cover the whole model, and reachability checks retain dependency-related invariant proofs and action-defect coverage. Unreleased: sliced selections report actions outside that coverage in selection.unassessed_actions. Unrelated defects encountered during exploration go into model_findings with model_coverage, outside the selected verdict. An unfiltered run still aggregates all checks and defects.
