See the CLI selection contract for supporting checks, scenario/tag compatibility and trace settings. A static shared model for two flows and cross-flow properties is in benchmarks/shared_checks.py.

0.2.0: repeated checks and traces observe edits to nested invariant expressions and lists as well as replacement of the whole expression. Compiled invariant checks and applicability plans live only for one synchronous exploration or verification scan; they are not stored on declarations or carried into model copies. Do not edit a model during a running check. A shallow Python or model_copy() copy still shares its nested declarations; changing them also changes the original. This repair does not re-expand parameter families or add newly referenced entities to an existing Spec automatically; see parameterized actions.

A second example, benchmarks/independent_checks.py, has an independent failed invariant: selecting safe_a succeeds while the full check fails. The report preserves the B findings without treating them as a failure of A's selected check.

docs.title: Fulfillment requirement-change trial
docs.text:
This trial uses the 0.1.0 check-selection API.

This repository-example trial exercises check selection with one shared model. The baseline customer cancellation window closes at payment capture. The additive hypothesis permits cancellation while the shipment is in transit, with cancellation and refund in one atomic model action. Cancellation after delivery is rejected. The original pre-dispatch cancellation policy remains.

Run from the repository checkout:

uv run python scripts/trial_fulfillment.py --output /tmp/fulfillment-trial
uv run analint check examples/fulfillment \
  --what-if benchmarks/fulfillment_cancellation.py \
  --check flow:cancel_in_transit --check query:no_money_for_nothing \
  --max-states 20000 -f json

The runner leaves the baseline example unchanged. It saves the baseline inspection, exact before/after/control hypotheses, full and compact reports, CLI exit codes, witnesses with state changes, and a source-hashed summary under --output. CI compares fresh verdicts, per-query state counts, flow outcomes and action counts with the committed measurement record. Timings, byte sizes and historical source metadata are excluded. If behavior intentionally changes, review and update both the record and this guide; do not regenerate the baseline merely to make CI pass. The same guard runs from the source archive against the built wheel. The extended model is an additive what-if revision, not a new root for each flow. Within each revision, all selections reuse the same prepared Spec; the runner checks membership identity and unchanged declarations. Every original action is retained, including delivery, loss and compensations.

Model revision Full check Selected flows Selected payment safety States per property Baseline PASS No flows declared PASS in full run 34 Old model plus new requirement probes FAIL Cancellation fails; delivery passes PASS 34 Cancellation with atomic refund PASS PASS separately and together PASS 36 Above plus an alternative cancellation without refund FAIL PASS separately and together FAIL 38

The old-model probe fails because the new journey is blocked, not because the old model is inconsistent. The negative control adds cancel_without_refund outside both flows. Property exploration finds it after supplier_restock → reserve_stock → authorize_payment → confirm_order → capture_payment → dispatch → cancel_without_refund. The order is cancelled while payment stays captured; settlement_always_reachable also fails because no recovery is possible. Both explicit flows still pass: their coverage is executed_steps_only. The control intentionally has one structural.no_scenarios warning; that warning is retained and is not the cause of the non-strict FAIL.

All 44 cases agree between sliced and whole-model verification at a 20,000-state budget. CLI/library results, check/trace action paths, and cold/warm cache reports also agree (excluding timings and the requested cache-option metadata). The passing selected safety proof needs no supporting invariant; the failing control falls back to the constrained path with delivered_means_paid as support. No query is INCONCLUSIVE and no original action is removed.

The model is coupled: selection still explores 36 states in the passing revision. One local Python 3.14 run took about 4.3 ms for full validation, 4.0 ms for the safety selection, and 1 ms per individual flow, excluding preparation. These are single observations, not a speedup claim. Compact output was slightly larger on these small reports. See the committed measurement record for source hashes and all measurements.

Bounds: one order, one payment, one shipment and a warehouse capacity of two. Refund is atomic with cancellation; payment-provider latency, physical returns, continued carrier activity after cancellation, retries and concurrent orders are outside the model. NoDeadEnd establishes reachable settlement, not eventual completion. This is an invented repository example and does not close the external real-spec trial or establish production conformance. No engine change or new DSL primitive was needed.

docs.title: Your first spec
docs.text: This example models one support ticket and a queue counter. Resolving the ticket must decrement the counter; only a resolved ticket can be archived. The finite model has three reachable states.

docs.title: Install and declare the model
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 or newer:

pip install analint
mkdir ticket_spec
cd ticket_spec

Save the complete program below as spec.py. The documentation checks execute this exact block, including the defect exercise later on this page.

spec.py
from enum import StrEnum

from analint import (
    Action, Assert, Entity, Expect, Field, Flow, Implies, Invariant,
    Lifecycle, NoDeadEnd, Reachable, Scenario, Set, Spec, Subtract,
)


class Status(StrEnum):
    NEW = "new"
    RESOLVED = "resolved"
    ARCHIVED = "archived"


class Ticket(Entity):
    status: Status = Lifecycle(
        initial=Status.NEW,
        transitions={
            Status.NEW: [Status.RESOLVED],
            Status.RESOLVED: [Status.ARCHIVED],
        },
        terminal=[Status.ARCHIVED],
    )


class Queue(Entity):
    open_tickets: int = Field(1, ge=0, le=1)


resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket = Invariant(
    Implies(Ticket.status != Status.NEW, Queue.open_tickets == 0),
    label="Resolving the only ticket clears the queue counter",
)

resolve = Action(
    pre=[Ticket.status == Status.NEW],
    effect=[
        Set(Ticket.status, Status.RESOLVED),
        Subtract(Queue.open_tickets, 1),
    ],
)

archive = Action(
    pre=[Ticket.status == Status.RESOLVED],
    effect=[Set(Ticket.status, Status.ARCHIVED)],
)

resolve_new = Scenario(
    action=resolve,
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    then=[Ticket.status == Status.RESOLVED, Queue.open_tickets == 0],
)

cannot_archive_new = Scenario(
    action=archive,
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    expected=Expect.FAIL,
)

ticket_journey = Flow(
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    steps=[
        resolve,
        Assert(Queue.open_tickets == 0),
        archive,
        Assert(Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED),
    ],
)

can_archive = Reachable(Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED)
archive_stays_possible = NoDeadEnd(goal=Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED)

spec = Spec(
    id="tickets",
    name="Ticket workflow",
    actions=[resolve, archive],
    invariants=[resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket],
    scenarios=[resolve_new, cannot_archive_new],
    flows=[ticket_journey],
    queries=[can_archive, archive_stays_possible],
)

The model contains the behaviour explicitly listed on Spec. Its entity types and inline lifecycle are derived from those references. Variable names supply ids such as resolve and can_archive; defining another action without listing it does not add it to the model.

docs.title: Run and interpret the checks
docs.text:
analint check .
analint check . --format json

Both scenarios, the flow, the invariant and both queries pass. The overall JSON has schema: "analint.check/v1", verdict: "PASS" and passed: true; the command exits with code 0.

cannot_archive_new passes because the archive precondition rejects a new ticket before execution. Expect.FAIL checks an intended rejection; it does not excuse a broken effect, postcondition or assertion.

The scenario and flow start from their own given snapshots. Reachability and automatic invariant verification use the canonical model, which here starts from the field defaults: a new ticket and one open ticket. Exploration checks every enabled action order within that model.

docs.title: Inspect before editing
docs.text:
analint show -p .
analint show action resolve -p .
analint affects Queue.open_tickets -p .
analint trace can_archive -p .

show and affects return JSON. The trace reaches the archived state through resolve → archive, showing the counter and status changes. NoDeadEnd says archiving remains possible from every reachable state; it makes no scheduling promise that a user will actually perform those actions.

docs.title: Introduce a defect
docs.text:
Delete this one effect from resolve:

Subtract(Queue.open_tickets, 1),

Run the check again:

analint check .
analint trace resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket -p . --format json

The check now fails with exit code 1. The counterexample reaches a resolved ticket with Queue.open_tickets still equal to 1. The invariant trace names the property under its invariant key and shows resolve as the violating step. The invariant-invalid state is retained as evidence and has no outgoing transitions. Restore the removed effect and check that the model passes again.

docs.title: Test a proposed rule without changing the model
docs.text:
First make the spec a Python package so that the checker and hypothesis share the same entity classes. From inside ticket_spec, create an empty __init__.py, then return to its parent directory:

touch __init__.py
cd ..

Save this separate file as hypothesis.py alongside the ticket_spec directory:

hypothesis.py
from analint import Invariant
from ticket_spec.spec import Queue

queue_is_always_empty = Invariant(Queue.open_tickets == 0)

Then check it against the restored model:

analint check ticket_spec --what-if hypothesis.py
analint trace queue_is_always_empty -p ticket_spec --what-if hypothesis.py

This hypothesis fails at the initial state: the new ticket is still open. The extra module is merged for this run; spec.py is unchanged. Scratch files outside the spec directory do not cause unloaded-file warnings on normal checks. Import shared types by their package name; importing a standalone entry as a second module can create different entity identities.
